summary.headline: NDR Auto Q2 FY27 revenue INR247.86 crore with 11.08% EBITDA margin; consolidated order book up to INR1,190 crore.
summary.overview: Management reported Q2 FY27 revenue of INR247.86 crore, EBITDA of INR27.47 crore (11.08% margin) and PAT of INR19.78 crore. Consolidated order book rose to INR1,190 crore (INR1,150 crore standalone, INR40 crore NDR Hayashi JV), driven mainly by Maruti Suzuki, Suzuki two-wheeler and new Toyota business. A 51% JV with Korea's DYA was announced (INR62.96 crore investment) targeting Hyundai and Kia full seat assemblies with INR800-1,000 crore of business expected in FY31. Management reiterated an INR3,000 crore revenue ambition by FY30 but gave no annual guidance; EBITDA margin was pressured by Haryana minimum wage hikes.

financial_highlights.value: 11.08% (management statement); analyst cited ~9.7% for the quarter, not disputed
INR1,190 crore (standalone INR1,150 crore; NDR Hayashi JV INR40 crore)

financial_highlights.change: up ~2.5x QoQ per analyst; management says sustainable
Haryana minimum wage hike ~INR2.5 crore; NDR South job work ~INR2.5 crore

financial_highlights.value: INR3.84 crore; includes ~INR2.7 crore from NDR South job work

segments.name: Seating (standalone)
segments.commentary: Predominant part of order book and revenue; seat covers and seat frames supplied to Maruti Suzuki, Kia and others. Management says seat frames and fabric supply continues in standalone entity.

segments.name: Non-seating auto components
segments.commentary: Order wins include Toyota business and sunshades (OEM-fitted door heat-protection parts) still under discussion with more OEMs; some order wins from 2-wheeler segment.

segments.name: NDR Hayashi JV
segments.commentary: Order book INR40 crore; orders from Toyota, with Maruti Suzuki models and other OEM presentations in progress.

segments.name: DYA JV (51% NDR)
segments.commentary: Proposed full seat assemblies for Hyundai Kia; INR62.96 crore investment; to be fully consolidated; production targeted FY31 with INR800-1,000 crore business and 1-1.5 lakh volume, content per vehicle INR50,000-80,000.

guidance_outlook: No annual guidance given; management said H2 margins should be similar to H1, with similar to slightly improved H1-on-H1 trajectory depending on model mix.
INR3,000 crore revenue ambition targeted by FY30: current top line INR900-1,000 crore plus INR1,150 crore standalone order book plus INR800-1,000 crore DYA JV in FY31; further initiatives under way.
Management expects EBITDA around 11% sustainable and hopes to return to ~11% from Q3; new capacity ramp expected to be slightly better next year.
New standalone seat-related ramp-ups: NDR South started, more models at end of year, seat belt reminder and seat programmes early next year.
Management said most of the INR1,150 crore order book will be executed by FY30, with FY29 and FY30 bigger years; no split by year provided yet.
capex_capacity: Board approved brownfield expansion at Gujarat and Kharkhoda plants for seat frames, trim and other auto ancillaries; new capex announced is for Maruti only.
Projects announced worth ~INR60 crore; JV capex another ~INR60 crore plus yearly maintenance capex (INR120 crore total cited for INR1,000-3,000 crore step-up).
CWIP INR39 crore including Latch seat belt reminder system project and other standalone capex; expansions expected around January 2027.
Land acquired at Aurangabad for NDR Hayashi JV plant; Toyota business at Aurangabad to be announced later.
demand_pricing: Raw material price increases are mostly passed on to customers with no lag, per management.
Analyst-sought price vs volume split for Q2 not available on call; management to share later.
Competition: Gabriel India announced JV with Forvia; management said this makes it tougher to win new OEMs but it is confident of retaining Maruti Suzuki share and entering Kia and Hyundai.
Company currently sells only in India; no exports yet, though export initiatives are being worked on.
Associate Toyo Seats (TSIL) turned profitable; share of associate profit ~INR5.2 crore per quarter, described as sustainable; price increases from customers reduced losses at NHI.

qa_highlights.question: Which customers make up the INR500 crore order book increase, and what size is expected from the DYA JV?
qa_highlights.answer: Mainly Maruti Suzuki and Suzuki two-wheeler, plus new Toyota business; DYA JV estimated at INR800-1,000 crore executed in FY31.

qa_highlights.question: What caused the dip in consolidated profit versus standalone PBT, and what is the nature of other income?
qa_highlights.answer: Standalone includes BSL dividend which is eliminated on consolidation; other income of ~INR2.7 crore arises from NDR South job work (manpower/rent) with matching expenses of ~INR2.5 crore, netted off.

qa_highlights.question: Is the Haryana minimum wage hike the reason for higher other expenses, and will margins return to 11-12%?
qa_highlights.answer: Yes, Haryana minimum wage hike drove the increase (about INR2.5 crore of the QoQ rise is NDR South, balance Haryana wages); management hopes for ~11% margin from Q3 with cost measures.

qa_highlights.question: Is the INR60 crore capex sufficient for the INR1,150 crore order book?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the capex supports the INR1,150 crore order book and uses some existing capacity, so it is not incremental to that book.

qa_highlights.question: Will the DYA JV's INR800-1,000 crore include Hyundai and is it combined seat value?
qa_highlights.answer: Only Kia is counted in the INR800-1,000 crore (about INR50,000-80,000 content per vehicle); Hyundai to be estimated later. Figure is combined seat value including company-supplied frames and fabric.

qa_highlights.question: Can management give FY27/FY28 guidance or an SOP split of the order book?
qa_highlights.answer: No annual guidance; management will revert on the order-book SOP split and ramp-up schedule for the next three years.

risks_watch: Haryana minimum wage increase keeps other expenses elevated; watch whether EBITDA margin recovers to ~11% in Q3.
Order book ramp-up timing unknown; management has no year-wise split and said last-minute delays happen.
DYA JV execution (FY31 production target, Hyundai/Kia dependence) and JV profitability below standalone margins.
Increased competition from Gabriel-Forvia JV for OEM seating business.
Pending pass-through of manpower cost increases to OEMs, still under negotiation.
summary.management_tone: Confident on the long-term order book and the INR3,000 crore ambition, but cautious and often deferring on specifics: no annual guidance, several answers promised later (price/volume split, SOP schedule, FY27-28 ballpark).
key_quotes: Our EBITDA margins remained healthy at 11.08% despite the environmental and supply chain challenges, which is a reflection of the efficiency of our operations.
We do not give annual guidance.
We are mostly able to pass on the raw material prices to our customers.
We will achieve the INR2,000 organic from it.

adds.what: Brownfield expansion at Gujarat and Kharkhoda plants for seat frames, trim and auto ancillaries (Maruti-related capex)
DYA JV full seat assembly plant for Hyundai/Kia (51% NDR, INR62.96 crore investment), production targeted FY31

growth.why: No annual guidance; management reiterates INR3,000 crore FY30 aspiration backed by INR1,150 crore standalone order book (executed mainly FY29-FY30) and INR800-1,000 crore DYA JV business in FY31, with ~90% utilisation and a ~INR60 crore announced capex plus ~INR60 crore JV capex, though no annual split or new-capacity timing beyond ~January 2027 was given.

rows.label: Margin expansion
rows.why: Management hopes to return to ~11% EBITDA margin from Q3 and says H2 margins should be similar to H1 (Q2 at 11.08% per management, ~9.7% per analyst), but Haryana minimum wage hike (~INR2.5 crore) and NDR South job work costs (~INR2.5 crore) weigh on other expenses that rose ~INR5 crore QoQ.

rows.label: Capacity expansion / commissioning
rows.why: Expansions in CWIP (INR39 crore) expected around January 2027 and new capacity ramp slightly better next year, but the INR60 crore announced capex is said to use some existing capacity; DYA JV plant production only targeted FY31.

rows.label: Volume growth
rows.why: Consolidated order book at INR1,190 crore (standalone INR1,150 crore) mainly from Maruti Suzuki, Suzuki two-wheeler and new Toyota business, with most of it executed by FY30 and FY29-FY30 bigger years; utilisation already ~90%.

rows.label: New capex announcement
rows.why: Utilisation at ~90% across plants with the INR60 crore brownfield programme approved and a further ~INR60 crore JV capex, but management has not guided to a new standalone capex beyond the approved Gujarat/Kharkhoda expansion.

rows.label: Guidance upgrade
rows.why: No annual guidance was given and management deferred FY27/FY28 ballpark and SOP split to later, while margins are under pressure from wage costs; the INR3,000 crore FY30 figure is explicitly aspirational.

rows.label: Guidance downgrade
rows.why: Analysts flagged margin pressure (~9.7% per analyst vs 11.08% claimed) and management admitted last-minute ramp delays happen, with no year-wise order book split yet.

rows.label: New product launch
rows.when: end of FY27 to early FY28
rows.why: Management flagged more models at NDR South by year-end, seat belt reminder and seat programmes early next year, plus sunshades and Toyota business still under discussion with more OEMs.

rows.label: DYA JV full seat assemblies for Hyundai/Kia
rows.why: 51% JV with INR62.96 crore investment targets INR800-1,000 crore business (Kia counted) executed in FY31 with 1-1.5 lakh volume, though production is far beyond the 2-4 quarter window.

rows.label: Toyota and Suzuki two-wheeler order wins
rows.why: Consolidated order book rose by about INR500 crore QoQ to INR1,190 crore, mainly Maruti Suzuki, Suzuki two-wheeler and new Toyota business; Toyota Aurangabad business to be announced later.

rows.label: Pass-through of raw material and manpower cost increases
rows.why: Raw material increases are passed on with no lag per management, but manpower cost pass-through to OEMs is still under negotiation after the Haryana wage hike of ~INR2.5 crore.

tone.note: Management was confident on the INR1,190 crore order book, the INR3,000 crore FY30 aspiration and sustainable ~11% margin, but cautious and deferring on annual guidance, price/volume split and SOP schedule; analysts pressed on margin (~9.7% vs 11.08%), other expense jump and whether the DYA JV count
